# Walkthrough

## Problem

Typing in any prose buffer — most visibly `journal.org` — spams this on every corfu-auto idle cycle:

```
Corfu detected an error:
  ...
  error("ispell-lookup-words: No plain word-list found at systemdefault locations.  Customize `ispell-alternate-dictionary' to set yours.")
  ispell-lookup-words("thhas")
  ispell-completion-at-point()
  corfu--capf-wrapper(ispell-completion-at-point 3)
```

A hack from 2025-05-25 (`ispell-program-name` = `"echo"` in `coding/init-corfu`) was supposed to stop this and did not.

## Root cause (each link verified against the Emacs 30.1 sources in the devenv)

1. **Emacs 30 changed a default.** `text-mode` now registers `ispell-completion-at-point` in `completion-at-point-functions` of every text-mode-derived buffer — org-mode included — because the new option `text-mode-ispell-word-completion` defaults to `completion-at-point` (`text-mode.el:155-156`). Nothing in this config enables it; the capf is baked into the buffer **once, at mode activation**.
2. **The capf is eager.** `ispell-completion-at-point` calls `ispell-lookup-words` immediately (`ispell.el:3726`), which requires a plain word-list *file* and **signals an error** when none exists (`ispell.el:2555`).
3. **Discovery is FHS-only.** `ispell-alternate-dictionary` probes `/usr/dict/web2`, `/usr/share/dict/words`, … (`ispell.el:208-216`). None exist on NixOS. The word list the system *does* ship — `environment.wordlist.enable = true` (`dotfiles/nixos/shared/common.nix:517`) exposes SCOWL via `$WORDLIST` — is never probed.
4. **corfu-auto surfaces it loudly.** With `corfu-auto t`, the capf chain runs on every idle cycle; corfu wraps it in `handler-bind` → `corfu--debug`, printing the backtrace each time.

**Why the old hack could not work:** word lookup greps the word-list file directly (`look`/`grep`, `ispell.el:2559-2564`) and never launches the spell-checker program, so `ispell-program-name` is irrelevant to the failing path — reproduced in batch Emacs: the error fires with the hack active. Meanwhile the hack *did* break flyspell (which `technical-writing/post-init-flyspell` enables in these same text/org/markdown buffers) by pointing the checker at `echo` instead of the aspell that `common.nix:397-400` installs.

## The change

Two files:

- **`dotfiles/emacs/.spacemacs`** — `tmrts/configure-ispell-word-lookup`, one commented defun holding the whole policy, called from `dotspacemacs/user-init` (which owns the timing: per link 1 the option must flip before the first text-mode buffer exists):
  1. `setopt text-mode-ispell-word-completion nil` — dictionary popups on every idle cycle are noise, each an eager synchronous subprocess; disabling is also upstream corfu's recommendation. (`setopt` because the option's `:set` function also updates `text-mode-map`: for nil it removes the `C-M-i` binding; `ispell-complete-word` stays reachable via `M-x`.)
  2. Once ispell loads, point `ispell-alternate-dictionary` at a readable `$WORDLIST` — deliberate lookups then serve the system word list instead of erroring. Resolution defers to ispell load time because Spacemacs imports the session environment (`~/.spacemacs.env`, `dotspacemacs/user-env`) only *after* user-init (`core-spacemacs.el:198` vs `:266`). Machines without `$WORDLIST` keep ispell's stock probing.
- **`dotfiles/emacs/.emacs.layers/coding/packages.el`** — removes the `"echo"` hack from `coding/init-corfu`; with it gone, `ispell-program-name` discovery finds aspell again and flyspell works.

No NixOS change needed — `common.nix` already ships the word list; Emacs just never looked at it.

## Process and divergences

- Red first: reproduced the exact error in batch Emacs 30.1 (empty `/usr/share/dict` in the devenv mirrors NixOS), with the old hack active — proving it inert — in both `text-mode` and `org-mode` buffers.
- The fix passed through two review-driven shapes — a layer-local module with an ERT suite (CIA-8 test-reachability blocker), then a reified user-init bootstrap helper (CIA-7.2 duplication finding) — before owner feedback set the abstraction level: a dedicated package for a two-setting policy is not worth its reader/maintenance cost. `b6c3520` collapses everything back into the `.spacemacs` defun; the module's test suite left with it (`.spacemacs` configuration carries no harness coverage in this repo, matching precedent — the executable verification below stands in).
- Every shape was held to the same outcome assertions in batch Emacs, with and without `$WORDLIST`: no ispell capf registered in text/org buffers, prose completion never signals, `$WORDLIST` feeds deliberate lookup once ispell loads, absent `$WORDLIST` preserves stock discovery.
- Test-suite parity: `./run-tests.sh` at baseline — 6 pass / 2 fail, the two `ai/` failures (`cognition-test.el`, `trace-labels-test.el`) failing identically on a clean checkout and untouched by this diff.

## Out of scope, for the record

- The `org-element--cache-sync: Invalid search bound (wrong side of point)` line in the original report is a separate org-mode cache defect that co-fires on a timer while editing; it is not caused by ispell/corfu. If it persists, `M-x org-element-cache-reset` in the affected buffer is the usual remedy; recurring cases are an org bug to chase independently.
- `technical-writing/packages.el:47` disables a jupyter-repl company backend citing "corfu errors" (2025-10-03) — different mode (not text-derived), likely unrelated; left alone, possibly worth revisiting.

feat[mve]: admit symbols after 30 days of history instead of 60

[PROBLEM]
min_symbol_maturity=60 withheld a symbol's first 60 days from the cross-sectional
ranking pool, and therefore from universe_days, and therefore from the sample. It
was set on the assumption that early-life data is unreliable. That assumption was
never tested, and it costs setups: six resolved trades sit in the 31-60 day band
and were being discarded.

[CAUSE]
min_symbol_maturity appears in exactly one place — the eligibility mask in
compute_membership. It never reaches process_symbol, so it is a pure
days-since-listing cut applied to trades after the fact, not a guard on how they
were computed.

The guard it was standing in for already exists, upstream, in the indicators:

  - range.2w is NaN until 14 days of bars accumulate, and detect_capitulations
    tests `confirm(range.2w).fillna(0) > min_price_range` — so it cannot fire.
  - r:adr.31d is built with min_periods=1, so during a symbol's first month it
    averages that symbol's launch days, when ranges are widest. That inflates the
    denominator of move_over_adr = log(max_high/first_open) / r:adr.31d and pushes
    it under its 0.5 threshold.

Empirically this is decisive: across a {0, 15, 30, 45, 60} sweep, no trade anywhere
lands earlier than 35 days since listing — not even at maturity=0. Below ~30 days
the gate is redundant with the indicator warmup. Above it, the gate was buying
nothing and paying six setups for it.

feat[emacs][agenda]: hand the clock back after friction and break captures

[PROBLEM]
Friction and break entries interrupt a clocked task.  With :clock-keep t
their capture leaves the clock running on the new entry, so after every
friction or break the interrupted task's clock must be restarted by hand
-- and is forgotten in practice, losing its time to the journal entry.

[CAUSE]
When these templates were introduced, the clock hand-back behavior was
locked to the fast journal capture key, so the closest available
approximation was to keep the clock on the captured entry.

[CHANGE]
Declare :clock-in t :clock-keep nil :resume-clock t on both templates
(the same lifecycle the fast journal capture uses): the entry is clocked
while being written, and on finalize the clock returns to whatever was
running when the interruption happened.  Verified end-to-end in a batch
session: during a friction capture the clock sits on the friction entry,
after finalize it is back on the interrupted task, and the entry retains
its closed CLOCK span.
